# Conduct and Confidentiality
## How we expect you to behave Whenever you're on site, you represent Weyland-Yutani. Colonists, visitors and officials will judge the Company by how you behave. - Be polite and professional, even when other people aren't. - Wear your uniform and keep it clean and tidy. - Treat your colleagues with respect. If there's a problem between you and another member of staff, take it to the Liaison rather than letting it grow. - Keep alcohol and personal business out of working hours.
## Confidentiality Much of what you see and hear at work belongs to the Company. That includes the site's accounts, its trade, its correspondence and anything to do with research. - Don't discuss Company business with anyone outside the Company, including colonists, friends and family. - Don't take documents or data out of the office. - If you overhear something you shouldn't have, keep it to yourself. - If someone outside the Company asks you about our work, politely say you can't comment and refer them to the Corporate Liaison.
Breaking confidentiality is a serious matter and may cost you your job.
## The colony The Company works on the colony's land in partnership with the colonial administration. A good relationship benefits everybody, so please be courteous to colonists and their officials. Only the Liaison and site management may make promises or agreements on the Company's behalf.
## Gifts and favours Don't accept gifts, money or favours from anyone you deal with at work. If someone offers you something, thank them, decline it, and let the Liaison know.
## Weapons Office staff don't carry weapons. Keeping the site safe is Corporate Security's job, not yours.
## Raising a concern If you're worried about something at work, speak to the Liaison. If your concern is about the Liaison, speak to Company counsel or the senior employee on site.
